definitionOfDone: All linked stories meet their acceptance criteria and are Done.
The linked QA task passed and its evidence is recorded.
No open blocking bugs or unresolved dependencies remain.
Unit and integration tests pass on the release candidate.
Release notes, operational impact, and rollback or flag-off plan are reviewed.

sprints.name: Sprint 1
sprints.goal: Deliver reliable order creation, checkout, payment capture, and retry paths.

sprints.name: Sprint 2
sprints.goal: Allocate inventory and complete fulfillment, shipping, tracking, and cancellation safely.

sprints.name: Sprint 3
sprints.goal: Complete self-service returns, controlled rollout, QA readiness, and Jira visibility.

epics.name: Order Creation & Checkout
epics.devTask: Implement order and checkout APIs with persistence and validation

stories.summary: As a customer, I want to review my cart and place an order so that I can begin a purchase with confidence.
ac: A valid customer and one or more available products create an order.
The order begins in CREATED and enters PAYMENT_PENDING.
The response provides an order ID and current status.

stories.summary: As a customer, I want to see an accurate order total before payment so that I know what I will be charged.
ac: The total equals the sum of unit prices multiplied by quantities.
Invalid quantities and unavailable products are rejected.
The total is persisted with the order.

stories.summary: As a customer, I want an order timeline so that I can understand progress without contacting support.
ac: The timeline shows every transition in chronological order.
Each entry shows status, actor, and timestamp.
Invalid transitions never appear in the timeline.

epics.name: Payment Processing
epics.devTask: Implement mock gateway adapters and durable payment attempt records

stories.summary: As a customer, I want to pay by card or wallet so that I can use my preferred payment method.
ac: CARD and WALLET are accepted payment methods.
A successful capture records amount, method, reference, and time.
Only captured payments advance the order to PAID.

stories.summary: As a customer, I want to retry a declined payment within a configured limit so that a temporary payment problem does not lose my order.
ac: A decline moves the order to PAYMENT_FAILED and records the attempt.
A retry moves through PAYMENT_PENDING and respects the configured maximum.
Inventory is not allocated until capture succeeds.

stories.summary: As a support agent, I want captured payments and refunds recorded so that I can reconcile customer payment outcomes.
ac: Successful captures and refunds create separate immutable attempt records.
Refund references are linked to the order.
Failed or invalid transitions do not create a false refund record.

epics.name: Inventory & Fulfillment
epics.devTask: Implement locked inventory allocation and fulfillment queue operations

stories.summary: As an admin, I want inventory allocated only after payment succeeds so that unpaid orders cannot reserve stock indefinitely.
ac: Successful payment allocates the requested quantity.
Failed payment leaves allocated quantity unchanged.
Concurrent checkout cannot allocate more than available stock.

stories.summary: As an order team member, I want a fulfillment queue of allocated orders so that warehouse work is clear and actionable.
ac: The queue includes INVENTORY_ALLOCATED and FULFILLING orders.
Starting fulfillment moves only allocated orders to FULFILLING.
Order items and quantities are visible in the queue.

stories.summary: As an order team member, I want canceled pre-shipment orders to release inventory so that sellable stock is restored.
ac: Cancellation is accepted only before SHIPPED.
Allocated quantities are released exactly once.
Stock counts remain consistent after cancellation.

epics.name: Shipping & Tracking
epics.devTask: Implement shipment transitions, tracking records, and delivery notifications

stories.summary: As an order team member, I want to add a tracking number when shipping an order so that delivery can be followed.
ac: Only FULFILLING orders may be shipped.
A tracking number is required and appears on the order.
Shipping consumes the allocated stock quantity.

stories.summary: As a customer, I want to look up my order and tracking status so that I can plan for delivery.
ac: The tracking view shows current status and tracking number when present.
The full order timeline is visible.
An unknown order returns a clear not-found response.

stories.summary: As a customer, I want a notification for every order status change so that I do not miss important updates.
ac: Each transition creates a simulated email/SMS log entry.
The recipient and timestamp are recorded.
Notification failure does not roll back a valid order transition.

epics.name: Cancellation, Returns & Refunds
epics.devTask: Implement cancellation rules, returned inventory handling, and refund operations

stories.summary: As a customer, I want to cancel an order before it ships so that I can stop an unwanted purchase.
ac: Cancellation succeeds before SHIPPED and is rejected after.
Allocated inventory is released.
A captured payment triggers a refund record.

stories.summary: As a customer, I want to request a return after delivery so that I can send back an item I do not want.
ac: Only DELIVERED orders may enter RETURN_REQUESTED.
The request appears in the order timeline.
Pre-delivery return requests are rejected.

stories.summary: As a support agent, I want to receive returned items and issue a refund so that the return lifecycle can be completed and audited.
ac: RETURN_REQUESTED can move to RETURNED and restock inventory.
Only RETURNED orders may be refunded.
The refund is recorded and the order ends REFUNDED.

epics.name: Release Management & Feature Flags
epics.devTask: Implement persistent feature flags and Jira-linked rollout guards

stories.summary: As a developer, I want feature flags stored in the database so that rollout state survives an application restart.
ac: Flags have a stable key, description, and enabled state.
Seed data is idempotent.
Flag state is available through the admin API.

stories.summary: As an admin, I want to enable or disable a feature flag so that I can control rollout without a code deployment.
ac: An authorized admin can toggle a known flag.
The new state is persisted and immediately visible.
Unknown flags return a clear error.

stories.summary: As a release manager, I want a feature flag linked to its Jira story and QA task so that incomplete work cannot be rolled out.
ac: Each managed flag stores a Jira issue key.
Enabling requires the story to be Done and linked QA work to pass.
Unavailable Jira data fails closed for flag changes but not for order processing.

stories.summary: As a developer, I want feature flags to default to off when Jira is unavailable so that unverified features cannot affect live order flow.
ac: When Jira cannot verify rollout readiness, the flag remains disabled.
Order processing continues while Jira is unavailable.
The admin UI explains why the flag could not be enabled.

epics.name: QA & Release Readiness
epics.devTask: Build readiness checks and lifecycle regression coverage

stories.summary: As a tester, I want automated lifecycle tests so that invalid state changes and payment regressions are caught before release.
ac: Tests cover valid and invalid state transitions.
Payment retry, cancellation refund, and return refund paths are tested.
The test suite runs with a clean H2 database.

stories.summary: As a tester, I want readiness checks for a Jira version so that I can explain whether the release can ship.
ac: The page groups issues by status and reports done versus total points.
Open blockers and unresolved dependencies are listed.
READY or NOT READY includes explicit reasons.

stories.summary: As a release manager, I want a Definition of Done checklist so that every release is assessed consistently.
ac: All stories and linked QA tasks must be complete.
Open blocking bugs and unresolved dependencies prevent readiness.
Green tests and release notes are part of the checklist.

epics.name: Jira Integration & Dashboard
epics.devTask: Implement resilient Jira client, operational bug deduplication, and project dashboard

stories.summary: As an admin, I want Jira release and sprint progress beside order metrics so that delivery work and live operations are visible together.
ac: The dashboard links to the Jira board and selected version.
Sprint progress shows completed and remaining story points.
Recent issues are listed when Jira is available.

stories.summary: As a support lead, I want a Jira bug created for repeated payment failures or stuck orders so that operational risks are tracked with context.
ac: A bug includes order ID, status, timestamps, and auto-created label.
An existing open bug for the same order is reused instead of duplicated.
A Jira outage does not interrupt order processing.

stories.summary: As a developer, I want Jira calls behind a replaceable interface so that the app can be tested offline and remain operational during Jira outages.
ac: Jira operations are accessed through an interface.
Tests can substitute a mock Jira client.
Timeout, rate-limit, and configuration errors are surfaced without failing core order actions.
